title: Pointless local aliases `labelStyle = traceDetailLabelStyle` and `modelDetail = detail`
description: `const labelStyle = traceDetailLabelStyle` (line 23) merely re-binds the module-level constant defined 5 lines above (line 18); `const modelDetail = detail` (line 24) is a no-op rename of the destructured prop. Both add an indirection layer with no behavioural or readability benefit — references could use `traceDetailLabelStyle` / `detail` directly, or `labelStyle` could simply BE the module constant's name. Trivial, but it is needless aliasing in an otherwise tightly-written component.
evidence: Line 18 `const traceDetailLabelStyle = { ... }`; line 23 `const labelStyle = traceDetailLabelStyle`; line 24 `const modelDetail = detail`. `modelDetail` is then threaded through modelScorePrediction(modelDetail), modelScoreFeatureColumns(modelDetail), etc., where `detail` would read identically.
behavior_preservation: Identical: aliases are referentially equal to their targets; inlining changes no runtime value.
